messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency > 2.3s for /v1/stream generation (us-west-2). Detected at 2026-03-17T14:12:34Z. Pager: @sara
sara: oncall — investigating, pulling realtime dashboards
sara: p95 around 420ms but p99 jumped to ~2.6s, streaming stalls at tail
chris: looking at KV cache metrics and eviction logs, saw mass evictions starting 14:10
chris: running: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serving | grep KVCacheEvict`
chris: sample output: ```Mar 17 14:10:12 KVCacheEvict key=ctx_87 size=1.1GB
Mar 17 14:10:12 KVCacheEvict key=ctx_92 size=0.9GB``` (trimmed)
max: could be cache thrash + one large request pattern. any spike in long-context jobs?
amy: seeing a burst of long-context /stream requests from partner partner-omega (10.1.42.*) around 14:09–14:11
max: can we route a fraction to smaller model (non-streaming) as a quick fallback?
amy: preparing canary: redwood-small-8q non-streaming @ 10%
sara: applying route: `rb route set /v1/stream model=redwood-small-8q weight=10%` — doing now
ops-bot: Route update succeeded: 10% -> redwood-small-8q
chris: watching latency after shift
sara: quick infra check: some serving pods show high RSS, a couple restarted (kube events show OOMKilled around 14:11)
tune: checking autoscaler/GPU saturation — nodes did scale but lagged, GPU memory spike coincides with refills
tune: will check node autoscaler logs and pod restart reasons now
amy: temporary mitigation: throttle long-context requests for public tier to token_limit=1024 (applied)
max: also throttling partner-omega IP range for 5m to reduce load
sara: customer-impact summary: streaming degradation and some timeouts affected ~10% of requests during the spike window
chris: after 10% route shift + throttle, p99 trending down to ~1.8s but still above 2.0s SLO; tail events remain
sara: if not stable in next 10m we'll open a bridge and escalate to full incident call. creating incident bridge id inc-3311115555
amy: noted follow-ups for postmortem: adaptive KV cache sizing, eviction priority by session recency, and partner rate-limits
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall=sara, severity set to P2
sara: thanks team — continue monitoring. I'll update the status page if we return to SLO or if we need broader comms.
